about.title: San Pablo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: San Pablo sees a steady flow of traffic where I-80 meets local streets like San Pablo Avenue, Rumrill Boulevard, and 23rd Street, and public records show 94 injury collisions and 130 people hurt in the most recent final reporting year. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to bring more reported crashes, likely tied to commute traffic feeding onto the freeway. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the aftermath can bring medical bills, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster asking for a recorded statement. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we're a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in Contra Costa County who can review your situation. Acting early matters here, since evidence like skid marks, vehicle damage, and witness memories fade fast, and California's filing deadlines don't wait. Getting matched with someone who can start preserving your case costs you nothing upfront.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but if a government entity like a city or county is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your San Pablo crash before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces what you can collect. Insurance adjusters know this and often push injured drivers to say things in a recorded statement that shift more fault onto them.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still contest these amounts aggressively. Having someone document your injuries and losses early can matter more than people expect.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to reduce or deny your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my accident happened near I-80 or on a city-maintained road like Rumrill Boulevard?
How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free connection service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only collect a fee if you recover compensation.
